name: Sikafloor-359 AU
paste:
SIKAFLOOR®-359 AU: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-359 AU, April 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/sikafloor-359-au.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-359 AU where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. Sikafloor®-359 AU is a solvent based, hard wearing durable 2-part finish coat for Sikafloor Systems. Available as a pigmented finish, clear satin finish or clear gloss finish.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikafloor®-359 AU may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Carparks all levels
    - Aeronautical
    - Defence
    - Automotives
    - Garages

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-359 AU
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Polyurethane UV Stable Pigmented and Clear Resin Coating
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.03) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Excellent in mechanical and chemical resistance
    - UV stable
    - Use as a finish coats for Sikafloor Park Deck Systems
    - UV stable over Sikafloor epoxy ES, EB & ET systems
    - Internal / External application
    - Excellent Petrol, Diesel & Skydrol resistance
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Polyurethane
2.6 Appearance and colour.
    | Resin - Part A | Either Clear Gloss/Satin or Pre-Tin- |
    | ted in required colour |
    | Hardener - Part B | Transparent, Liquid |
    | Sikafloor®-359 AU is available in N45 Koala Grey and other RAL colours on request. |
    | ▪ Non standard colours can be supplied on request. (Check with Sika if additional cost applies) |
    | ▪ Refer to the Sikafloor epoxy colour chart for details |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.7 Density.
    | Clear | Pigmented |
    | Part A | ~ 0.95 kg/l | ~ 1.22 kg/l |
    | Part B | ~ 0.98 kg/l | ~ 0.98 kg/l |
    | Mix resin | ~ 0.96 kg/l | ~ 1.14 kg/l |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C.
2.9 Packaging.
    | Part A | 15 litres |
    | Part B | 5 litres |
    | A+B Kit | 20 litres |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment. The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull off strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm2. If in doubt apply a test area first.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Clear & Pigmented - Part A:Part B = 3:1 (by volume)
    - Consumption: Approx. 7-10 m2/litre/coat
    - Pot Life: Approx. 50 mins at ±23oC
    - Waiting time to overcoating: Approx. 4 hours at ±23oC
    - Applied product ready for use: Foot traffic: Approx. 24 hrs. at ±23oC; Heavy traffic: Approx. 48 hrs. at ±23oC
4.3 Mixing. Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A, mix continuously for 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved.
4.4 Application. Prior to application, confirm substrate moisture content, relative humidity and dew point. As a seal coat, the product can be applied by squeegee and then back-rolled (crosswise) with a short-piled roller.
4.5 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull off strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm2. If in doubt apply a test area first.
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Clear | Pigmented; Part A | ~ 0.95 kg/l | ~ 1.22 kg/l; Part B | ~ 0.98 kg/l | ~ 0.98 kg/l; Mix resin | ~ 0.96 kg/l | ~ 1.14 kg/l (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-359 AU, April 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/sikafloor-359-au.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikafloor 359 AU Part A, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/MSDS%20Sikafloor%20-%20359%20AU%20Part%20A%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-359 AU Part B, version 05/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sds-sikafloor-359aupartb.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
